title: ADAPT: Physics-Aware Diffusion-based World Models for Adaptive Predictive Transferable HVAC Control
abstract: arXiv:2608.19804v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Buildings account for roughly one-third of global energy consumption and CO$_2$ emissions. Optimizing indoor climate systems plays a critical role for urban climate mitigation aligned with UN Sustainable Development Goals 11 and 13. However, indoor delayed thermodynamic responses and partial observability severely hinder existing methods, which are primarily limited by implicit thermal inertia, occupancy dynamic prediction, and cumulative prediction errors, especially for out-of-distribution environments. In practice, these challenges are further exacerbated by the high cost and privacy burden of dense indoor sensing, forcing operators to collect only limited data in a single operating regime while expecting controllers to generalize reliably across unseen seasons and climate regions. translated_title: ADAPT：基于物理感知扩散的世界模型，用于自适应预测性可迁移的暖通空调控制
translated_abstract: 建筑约占全球能源消耗和二氧化碳排放量的三分之一。优化室内气候系统对于实现联合国可持续发展目标11和13中的城市气候缓解至关重要。然而，室内延迟的热力学响应和部分可观测性严重阻碍了现有方法，这些方法主要受限于隐式热惯性、占用动态预测和累积预测误差，尤其是在分布外环境中。实际上，这些挑战因高成本和密集室内传感的隐私负担而进一步加剧，迫使操作员仅在单一运行模式下收集有限数据，同时期望控制器能可靠地泛化到未见过的季节和气候区域。为解决此问题，我们提出了ADAPT，一种用于暖通空调控制的物理感知条件扩散室内环境世界模型。该模型预测一个...（摘要截断）
tldr: ADAPT提出了一种物理感知的条件扩散世界模型，通过显式建模热动力学和减少预测误差，实现了在有限数据和分布外环境下可靠的暖通空调控制泛化。
en_tdlr: ADAPT introduces a physics-aware conditional diffusion world model that explicitly models thermal dynamics and reduces prediction errors, enabling reliable HVAC control generalization under limited data and out-of-distribution environments.
